Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: HIPAA/SOC2 requirements & next steps

Hi Jamie / Tara,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear how Elara is planning to surface clinician notes and claims data into the clinical insights workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on deployment mode and security needs.

Recap from our discussion:
- Data classification: primary flows will include PHI (patient identifiers + notes).
- Key requirements: BAA in place, SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit logging for access, and control over data residency for certain customers.
- Performance: target 200 concurrent requests, ~250k tokens/day aggregate; 95th pct latency target ~ <500ms for short prompts.

Deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest to ship) — acceptable for non-PHI or pseudonymized data; lower cost but not suitable for workloads that require customer-managed keys or tight network isolation.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — provides data isolation per tenant and predictable throughput; good middle ground for PHI if combined with a BAA and strict access controls.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — required when customers require full network isolation, customer-managed KMS/HSM, or when a formal audit requires an on-prem footprint.

Requests / next steps from Elara:
- Can you confirm whether the initial scope will include PHI in production or whether you plan to pseudonymize?
- Please share the procurement contact and timeline for a BAA and contract review.
- It would be helpful if you can send any security questionnaire items up front.

Action items (from our side):
- I will loop in our security lead (cc'd Marissa) to provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a BAA template.
- If Elara leans to Dedicated or Private, we can prepare a short TCO sketch comparing Dedicated vs Private (networking, KMS, ops support).
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical + security deep dive next week to review controls and sample architecture.

If you can respond with PHI confirmation and procurement contact, I'll get the docs over by Monday.

Best,

Hi Jamie / Tara — looping in security/compliance docs and next steps.

Per Rishi's note, attached are the items we can share now:
- Attachment: SOC2_Type2_report_redacted.pdf — redacted report (control names and scope, no customer PII).
- Attachment: BAA_template_redwood.docx — our standard BAA; happy to iterate with your legal team.
- Attachment: deployment-checklist-dedicated-vs-private.xlsx — checklist covering KMS, network isolation, audit logs, and operating responsibilities for each deployment mode.

A few clarifications that should help your infra team:
- For Dedicated: tenant isolation + optional customer-managed KMS (supported providers: AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). Network isolation is via VPC peering + strict security groups; audit logs are forwarded to your secure storage on request.
- For Private VPC/on-prem: we can support direct integration with on-prem KMS/HSM and provide an on-site ops package for audits. This path has longer lead time and higher OPEX but is recommended if your auditors require physical separation.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Provide any vendor questionnaire answers you'd like us to return before the call.
2) Pick a time for a 45-min technical + security deep-dive (we have availability Wed 10/14 10am PT or Thu 10/15 11am PT).
3) If you want redlines to the BAA in advance, share your legal contact and we can turn around an initial set of comments within 3 business days.

Happy to join the call and walk through the SOC/controls and the deployment checklist.
